questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment. If no substitution is required select 'No substitution'.**

This is one of the boldest __economic reform that have ever__ been introduced.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'economic reforms that have ever.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **According to the rule,** **'one of' **is the phrase with this phrase use **'a plural noun'**
 
• **In the given underlined phrase, economic** is an **adjective** which is used to qualify a noun** 'reform'** hence, *according to the rule we need to use a plural noun i.e. reforms *
 
• *on the other hand, after this plural noun, a relative pronoun is used i.e. 'that' hence we need to use a verb in a plural form according to the antecedent rule.*
 
• ***Thus the correct sentence is- **This is one of the boldest economic reforms that have ever been introduced.​*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

***Now, let's look at the following points-***

 
• ***General structure - One of the + Subject (Plural) + Verb (singular)***
 
• But, when** one of the + plural + relative pronoun **the verb that follows the relative pronoun agrees in number with the word that comes immediately before the relative pronoun. 
 
• Therefore the verb used will be plural.

questions.question:

Please sign these documents ______ ink so that they can be preserved.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 4) i.e. 'in'.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****

__
 
• We always use the preposition 'in'__ when we describe some characteristic intrinsic to the writing itself.
 
• IN: To write in something (where 'in' denotes a method or style, not location or position) is to describe some characteristic intrinsic to the writing itself:
 __
 
• in cursive
 
• in Russian
 
• in Ink
 
 
 
• **The correct sentence:** "*Please sign these documents** in** ink so that they can be preserved.*"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

__
 
• You might get confused with in and with. But, there is a difference:
 
• WITH: To write with something (where 'with' indicates agency and not accompaniment) usually relates something about the writer, the writer's tools, or the writing process; I can write
 
 
• with a feather quill
 
• with a flourish
 
• with the memory still fresh in my mind
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Prepositions show the relationship between 2 words :

 
• **With-**- is used for instruments: "*She hit him with a stick.*"
 
• **By**-- is used for agents: "*It was written by a great poet."*
 
• **From**-- is used to show the starting point: "*The concert is from 6 p.m. onwards.*"

questions.solution:
**The option that has the error is option 2: and desiring to pursue her hobbies.**

**Desiring** is a **continuous form of the verb.** Based on the grammatical structure of the sentence, however, a **simple form** is required-- **desire.**

__Correct Sentence__: Among the reasons cited by the employee, for quitting the job, were the pressure of work, the outstation duties **and desire to pursue her hobbies.**

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.**

The monsoon have, in the past five days, retreated from most parts of the country.
questions.solution:
**The correct option is 1: The monsoon have. [ has the error].**

The verb always has to agree with the subject. In the given sentence, the subject is **'monsoon' which is singular.** So, the verb should be singular too.

**'Have'** is a **'perfect tense auxiliary'** for** plural** - instead, we should use **'has'**

__Correct sentence__: **The monsoon has, **in the past five days, retreated from most parts of the country.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

______ of these boys is doing anything worthwhile.
questions.solution:
**The correct option is 3. i.e. None.**

First, let us understand the meaning of the words:

 
• **Either**= one or the other.
 
• **Each**= everyone in a group.
 
• **None**= not one / not any.
 
• **Both**= two things identified together

 

The sentence has a singular verb 'is'. So, the subject word that fits the blank is -'None' [ it means 'no one' which is singular].-S+V+O [ subject-verb agreement].

**The correct option is 3-- None.**
